summary: Through Leading The Way I run Leadership Development, a twice-a-month class for young people and young professionals who've been handed responsibility, or want it, and nobody has shown them how. They find out where they're strong, where they're not, and how to make a decision when it counts.
audience: Young people and young professionals who are starting out and stepping up: a teen just made captain, a new shift lead now supervising friends, someone coming back from a setback. Managers and owners can have their young staff book their own free call. Anyone under 18 needs a parent on that call.
problem:
Before: "She got thrown into it." "They don't listen to me." "I don't know how to be the boss of my friends." They have the title, and they won't say they're struggling.
After: they know more about what makes them who they are, and they've practiced the harder part, keeping the role and the respect of the people they lead.
moments:
Named team captain this season
Promoted to shift lead and now supervising people they used to work beside
Cut, passed over, or ready to quit
A bad review at work
Young staff moving into lead roles
offerings:
Leadership Development, my twice-a-month class with Leading The Way
Finding out where you're strong and where you're not
Real situations, not a textbook: making a call under pressure and talking through what you'd do
Practice leading teammates or a crew, and getting back up after a setback
howItRuns:
Twice a month, every other Wednesday at 9 a.m., on Zoom. Which time zone that is, people can ask on the free call. It's calm, not a boot camp. I push them, and I'm on their side.
The free call is 15 minutes with the NowTRANSFORMED team, not with me, booked up to three weeks ahead. Anyone under 18 needs a parent on the call. After the call, if it fits, I send the joining details myself.
faqs:
Q: When does it meet?
A: Every other Wednesday at 9 a.m., so twice a month, on Zoom. Ask on your free call which time zone that is. If 9 a.m. on a Wednesday never works for you, this class may not be the right one.

Q: Who can join?
A: Young people and young professionals who are starting out. If you're not sure you're old enough, ask on your free call. Anyone under 18 needs a parent on that call.

Q: My son isn't really a leader type.
A: Most people aren't, until somebody shows them. He can sit in on the free call with you and hear it for himself. The class is for young people who want it, and I won't drag anyone.

Q: How do I know this is legitimate?
A: Fair question. I spent 30 years in the fire service, and Leading The Way is my business. The free call is run by NowTRANSFORMED, a youth leadership development program.

Q: How much does it cost?
A: You'll get the exact price on your free call.
aboutYou:
I spent 30 years in the American fire service. I led with a title and without one, and I learned how through years of formal education and countless hours on calls most people never have to see.

Now I run Leading The Way and teach what I learned to young people and young professionals.
mustNotSay:
No prices on the page.
Never promise a promotion, a scholarship or a captaincy.
Don't make it sound like a boot camp. Nobody's yelling.
Don't state the class time zone until it's confirmed.
